label: cs-enhancer-rank
topic: How promoter-specific are enhancer effects (rank-order changes)? Full-suite run on real Bergman et al. 2022 ExP STARR-seq barcode counts (GEO GSE184426)
summary:
Real data fetched now: GSE184426_ExP_1Kx1K_counts.txt.gz (6,214,483 barcode rows, 1000 promoters x 1014 enhancer ids, 826,005 promoter-enhancer cells, K562). Held-out split was preregistered by sha256 before any activity value was computed; the final evaluation ran once.

RESULT 1 (multiplicative model): fit on 453,797 development cells, it scores R^2 = 0.835 on 113,011 held-out cells (Pearson 0.914, RMSE 1.20 log2). Baselines: grand mean 0, promoter-only 0.567, enhancer-only 0.259. Shuffling enhancer labels before fitting drops R^2 to 0.565, i.e. to the promoter-only level, so the scorer does respond to broken input. The published figure, taken from the earlier literature agent's file and not from the paper itself, is 0.82.

RESULT 2 (rank flips, 203 whole held-out enhancers x the 50 best-covered promoters, 23.4 million enhancer-pair x promoter-pair comparisons):
- Raw discordant order: 17.9%. A pure multiplicative model plus the measured noise predicts 19.5%, so the raw discordance is fully explained by noise.
- Doubly significant comparisons (|z|>3 on both promoters): 1,051 of 2,678,362 are in opposite order (0.039%). The noise-only expectation is 24.9, a 42-fold excess. The Lean theorem allows 0 true reversals for any monotone single-strength model.
- Broken-input control (enhancer labels permuted within each promoter): 49.6% flips, as it should be.
- Median Spearman between promoters: 0.87 (minimum 0.23).

Reading: in this human dataset, real rank reversals exist, so the monotone-saturation class is not exactly true, but they are rare (about 4 in 10,000 well-measured comparisons). Multiplicative scaling is the dominant behaviour.

Biggest thing that was wrong: my first development rehearsal used replicate-only noise and gave a spurious 7.7% flip rate. The four RNA replicates share the same barcodes, so barcode-to-barcode noise (about 0.9-1.0 log2 standard error, against 0.08-0.4 from replicates) was invisible. I amended the noise model on development data, with a timestamp, before the held-out files were read. The earlier q1-data agent's 26.5% reversal figure on the mouse dataset used replicate-only noise and may be inflated for the same reason; I did not re-test that dataset.

The Lean files were read but not re-compiled in this run.

suite.case_name: Enhancer x promoter multiplicativity and rank-order flips (Bergman 2022 ExP STARR-seq, K562)
suite.statement: Law: log2 activity(p,e) = mu + a_e + b_p, i.e. activity = enhancer strength x promoter strength. Bound: tracks/research/lean/q1-theory-lean__EnhancerPromoterRank.lean (EPSpec.no_reversal_of_monotone) and q1-mechanisms__RankSaturation.lean (Q1.no_reversal) state that any model f(p,e) = h_p(a_e) with monotone h_p (multiplicative, log-additive, promoter-specific saturation) permits zero true strict rank reversals, so reversals beyond measurement noise falsify the whole class. I read both files but did not re-compile them in this run.
suite.holdout_set: Rule written to prereg.md at 2026-11-14T04:18:00Z (shell date -u), before any activity value was aggregated. (1) Whole enhancers with int(sha256(enhancer_id)[:8],16) % 5 == 0 are held out: 207 of 1014 enhancer ids, 169,655 cells. (2) Among the other enhancers, cells with sha256(promoter|enhancer) % 5 == 0 are held out: 130,641 cells (113,011 after the frozen quality filter). Development: 525,709 cells. Held-out cells were written to a separate file that only the final stage reads; the final stage ran once (timestamp in final_run_timestamp.txt).
suite.validation: Development only. A quality-filter grid on DNA_input minimum (50 to 800) gave replicate split-half r = 0.986-0.989 and inner cross-validated R^2 = 0.834-0.894; the preregistered rule chose 50 (453,797 cells). The noise model was first replicate SD by decile of read count. A flip rehearsal on 188 development enhancers x 50 promoters then gave 7.7% reversals against about 0 expected, which exposed the noise model as too optimistic. Amendment 1 (timestamped, before the held-out files were read) added a barcode-half standard error (0.64-1.04 log2). The rehearsal then gave 471 flips of 863,994 significant comparisons (0.055%) vs 9 expected, raw discordance 18.1% vs 19.5% null, and a permutation control at 50.2%.
suite.performance: Single final evaluation. Metric 1: held-out R^2 of the multiplicative model = 0.835 (n = 113,011 cells; Pearson 0.914; RMSE 1.20 log2). Baselines: grand mean 0.000, promoter-only 0.567, enhancer-only 0.259; published 0.82 as relayed by the earlier literature agent. Broken input (enhancer labels shuffled before fitting): R^2 falls to 0.565, so the scorer gets worse as it should. Metric 2: on 203 held-out enhancers x 50 promoters (9,929 cells; 23,437,464 enhancer-pair x promoter-pair comparisons), raw discordant fraction is 17.9% vs 19.5% under multiplicative + noise simulation. Among 2,678,362 comparisons significant at |z|>3 on both promoters, 1,051 are reversed (0.039%) vs 24.9 expected from noise (42-fold excess) and 0 allowed by the Lean theorem. Broken input (labels permuted within promoter): 49.6% reversed.
suite.what_was_wrong: 1. In the law: exact multiplicativity, and the whole monotone single-strength class, is falsified, since 1,051 significant reversals were seen where 0 are allowed and about 25 are expected from noise. The violation is small: 0.039% of well-measured comparisons, with 83.5% of held-out variance explained. 2. In my own run: the first noise model (SD across the 4 RNA replicates) was wrong because the replicates share the same barcodes; it gave a spurious 7.7% flip rate in the development rehearsal. It was fixed by a timestamped amendment before the held-out data were read. 3. The amended barcode noise is slightly too large: the null predicts 19.5% raw discordance vs 17.9% observed, and the additive residual SD of 0.85 is below the median SE of 0.97. The z>3 test is therefore conservative and the true flip rate may be somewhat higher. 4. The null assumes Gaussian noise, and heavy-tailed barcode outliers could produce part of the 42-fold excess; I did not test this. 5. Earlier agent work: q1-data reported 26.5% reversals among doubly-significant pairs on the mouse GSE186265 data using 'pooled replicate SD' as noise. That is the same class of noise model that failed here, so that figure may be inflated; I did not re-test it. 6. Earlier agent work: q1-critic's arccos(rho)/pi null was only simulated, and q1-literature relayed R^2 = 0.82 without a held-out re-computation; this run is the first held-out check and it agrees (0.835). 7. In the Lean files: the theorem is about noise-free values, and Q1.no_reversal is over natural numbers, so it gives no quantitative noise allowance; the comparison to data needs the simulated null, which is outside Lean. 8. In the data and pipeline: about 6 barcodes per cell on average and many low-count cells; I used raw reads with pseudocount 1, not the authors' weighted reads or Poisson model; scrambled control sequences were kept as ordinary enhancers and promoters; 1014 enhancer ids, not 1000; flips were tested only on the 50 promoters with most DNA input, so promoter-class effects among weak promoters are not covered. 9. The null used only 10 simulations. No simulated data were used for any performance number.

key_claims: On real human ExP STARR-seq data the multiplicative model explains 83.5% of held-out variance (promoter-only baseline 56.7%).
Raw rank discordance between promoters (17.9%) is fully accounted for by measurement noise (19.5% expected).
Significant rank reversals occur 42 times more often than noise predicts but make up only 0.039% of well-measured comparisons; the Lean theorem allows zero.
Replicate-only noise models overstate reversals by orders of magnitude when replicates share barcodes (7.7% vs 0.055% on development data).
lay_summary: Enhancers are DNA switches that turn genes up, and promoters are the start buttons of genes; we asked whether a strong switch is strong for every start button.
We used a real experiment that tested about a thousand switches with about a thousand start buttons, and hid one fifth of it before looking.
A simple rule, 'switch strength times button strength', predicted the hidden part well, getting about 84 percent of the variation right.
Switches almost always keep the same order from one button to the next; true order swaps happen, but only about 4 times in 10,000 clear comparisons.
We also learned that if you underestimate how noisy the measurement is, you see many fake swaps, which we caught and fixed before opening the hidden data.

glossary.enhancer: A stretch of DNA that boosts how much a gene is used.
glossary.promoter: The stretch of DNA at the start of a gene where reading begins.
glossary.multiplicative model: The idea that output equals one number for the enhancer times one number for the promoter.
glossary.rank flip (reversal): Enhancer A beats B on one promoter, but B beats A on another.
glossary.R^2: Share of the variation in the data that a model predicts; 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than guessing the average.
glossary.held-out set: Data hidden before the analysis and used only once at the end to score the model.
glossary.barcode: A short DNA tag that identifies each copy of a test construct; different tags give somewhat different readings.
glossary.z-score: A difference divided by its measurement error; above 3 means very unlikely to be chance.
glossary.monotone saturation: Output that rises with input and levels off, but never goes back down.
glossary.STARR-seq: A lab method that measures how strongly thousands of DNA pieces boost gene activity at once.
glossary.Spearman correlation: A measure of how similar two rankings are; 1 means the same order.

recommendations: Re-run the earlier q1-data analysis of GSE186265 with a barcode- or element-level noise estimate before quoting its 26.5% reversal figure anywhere.
Add a noise-aware statement to the Lean file (e.g. a bound on reversal probability under bounded noise) so the data comparison does not rest on simulation alone.
Break the 1,051 held-out reversals down by promoter class to test the published housekeeping vs variable-promoter compatibility claim; this needs a new preregistered split.

Extend the suite scorer convention: every rank-flip case must report the broken-input control and a noise null built from the lowest shared unit of measurement (here barcodes), not from replicates alone.
